note.note:
History:
- Main complaint: Swelling on the left elbow, first noticed about a week ago.
- Onset/duration: Swelling appeared approximately 7 days ago; has persisted since.
- Progression: No mention of enlargement or worsening; feels the same or slightly improved.
- Character: Swelling is described as “weird,” slightly warm, feels like fluid inside; not painful, though mild discomfort next to the swelling.
- Function: No limitation in movement; full range of motion; no pain with movement.
- Associated symptoms: No redness, no systemic symptoms (e.g., fever, malaise); no prior similar episodes.
- Context: No history of trauma, injury, repetitive movement, or physical work. Desk job. Active; runs 2-3 times per week.
- No family history of rheumatological diseases reported.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis (diagnosed by GP, several years ago).
- Allergic to peanuts.
- No known medication allergies.
- No regular medications.
- No other chronic illnesses or relevant past hospitalizations reported.

Physical Examination:
- Visible swelling over left olecranon region (elbow).
- Area is slightly warm to touch.
- Mild discomfort on palpation next to, but not at, the tip of the elbow.
- No significant redness.
- No significant tenderness; not very painful.
- No limitation of movement; able to fully move elbow.
- Skin over tip of elbow appears dry.
- No signs of systemic illness (alert, well-appearing).
- No other joint involvement reported.
- No throat swelling, no rashes elsewhere.
- No fever or chills.
- Relevant negatives: No trauma, no prior similar swelling.

Impression:
- Left olecranon bursitis, likely non-infectious (most consistent with transcript findings).
  - DDx supports: 1) Olecranon bursitis (non-infectious) – classic features described; 2) Early/inapparent septic bursitis or gout are less likely but will be ruled out with labs.

Management Plan:
- Initiated anti-inflammatory therapy: Ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily, after food (instructions provided; patient advised to stop if heartburn develops).
- Blood tests ordered (forms to be mailed): inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatological antibodies, uric acid/gout screen, etc.
- Advised to seek urgent re-assessment if swelling becomes very red, increasingly painful, or if redness spreads (emergency sign for septic joint).
- Arranged follow-up review after blood test results available (6–7 days), via clinic or telemedicine as convenient.
- Provided reassurance that the condition is not dangerous or life-threatening at this time.

Patient Summary:
- 53-year-old man presented with a week-long, non-painful swelling of the left elbow; no trauma, function preserved, slight warmth noted. Diagnosis of probable non-infectious olecranon bursitis was made. Started NSAID, blood work arranged, and close follow-up recommended.

Key Takeaways:
- Begin prescribed course of Ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily, after meals; discontinue if there is heartburn.
- Seek medical attention urgently if redness, severe pain, or rapid increase in swelling develops.
- Attend for blood tests as soon as the form arrives; arrange follow-up appointment afterwards.

Next Steps:
- Complete laboratory investigations as arranged.
- Book follow-up appointment to review clinical status and blood results (~1 week).
- If condition deteriorates (severe pain, redness, systemic illness), present for urgent reassessment.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements: No vital signs documented; no explicit review of all systems (other than musculoskeletal/skin); immunization status not recorded.
- No apparent conflicts between transcript and DDx.
- Transcript quality: Clear and complete for relevant history, exam, and plan; no significant inaudible sections.
